headline: GREENLAND BANS SEABED MINING IN UNANIMOUS VOTE — DIRECT REBUKE TO TRUMP'S MINERAL PUSH
snippet: Greenland's parliament passed a unanimous resolution to ban seabed mineral extraction on October 16, striking a direct contradiction with President Trump's announced plan for oil, gas and mineral exploration across the territory. The vote came the day after Trump's Greenland mineral initiative was publicized, highlighting the political fragility of Western mineral ambitions in the Arctic. The ban applies to offshore seabed extraction only — onshore projects such as Critical Metals' Tanbreez rare earth project are not directly affected — but the vote signals a hardening of Greenland's autonomous governance position on natural resource control at a politically charged moment for the entire sector.

headline: BLACKROCK'S HAMBRO SLAMS GOLD MINER BUYBACKS AS 'RECKLESS' — CALLS FOR EXPLORATION INVESTMENT
snippet: Evy Hambro, head of BlackRock's natural resources investment team and manager of the world's largest gold ETF allocation, publicly criticized gold mining companies at an October 16 conference for allocating capital to share buyback programmes 'without any real process,' calling the approach reckless at a time when the sector needs to invest in exploration and mine development to extend shrinking reserve lives. With gold near $4,170 per ounce — far above AISC for most producers — Hambro's remarks imply that miners are returning capital to shareholders rather than reinvesting in the asset base, a pattern that historically precedes production cliff-edges in the mid-cycle. The comments land during Q3 earnings season and directly challenge the narrative some producers have used to justify buybacks as shareholder-friendly capital discipline.

headline: SAN DIMAS SILVER MINE STRIKE ENTERS 6TH WEEK — OUTPUT DOWN 41%, NO DEAL IN SIGHT
snippet: Mexico's San Dimas silver mine — operated by First Majestic Silver and one of the country's largest primary silver producers — remains fully halted after 800 workers in two sections of the national miners' union escalated to a formal strike on October 8, following an initial work stoppage on September 18. Silver output at the mine had already fallen 41% year-over-year in Q3 2026, with the company attributing 12 lost operating days to the dispute. The union cites safety conditions, worn equipment, breaches of the labour contract and an unresolved productivity bonus. No settlement date has been set; a separate tax arbitration with the Mexican government was suspended until December 31, 2026 in an unrelated deal that does not resolve the labour dispute.

headline: WALL STREET SPLIT ON GOLD — SURVEY SHOWS 50% NEUTRAL AS $4,200 CEILING HOLDS FOR SECOND WEEK
snippet: Kitco's weekly sentiment survey found 33% of Wall Street analysts bullish on gold's near-term trajectory, 17% bearish, and 50% neutral — reflecting the market's inability to sustain a break above the $4,200 resistance ceiling for a second consecutive week. Main Street retail sentiment edged closer to a bearish majority after the latest failed breakout. Gold closed the week near $4,172 per ounce and silver near $57.63. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh declined Thursday to signal an October rate hike, providing modest late-week support; the October 27-28 FOMC meeting remains the next key directional catalyst. Key support sits at $4,148; analysts cite $4,602 as the next significant weekly-close target above.

headline: GOLD EYES SOFT US DATA FOR FED PAUSE SIGNAL — HOUSING, PMI AND CONSUMER SENTIMENT DUE
snippet: Kitco's October 16 weekly outlook identifies housing starts, weekly jobless claims, S&P Global PMI and University of Michigan consumer sentiment as the key data points shaping gold's direction into the October 27-28 FOMC meeting. Analysts expect softer readings to reinforce the Fed-pause thesis and provide a floor for gold above $4,148; stronger-than-expected data would solidify December hike expectations, keeping the dollar elevated and gold capped below $4,200. Escalating Middle East tension and rising crude oil prices are cited as a secondary inflation risk that could complicate Fed messaging regardless of incoming data. Gold held near $4,172, silver near $57.63, heading into the weekend.

headline: VALE: MIDDLE EAST COSTS PUSH 10% OF GLOBAL IRON ORE SUPPLY INTO LOSSES — 160M TONNES AT RISK
snippet: Vale's CEO said on October 16 that soaring energy and freight costs driven by the Middle East conflict have pushed approximately 10% of global iron ore supply — roughly 160 million tonnes of annual production — into economic losses, signalling that commodity cost inflation is now forcing structural supply reduction across multiple sectors. The observation applies directly to junior mining investors: if high-cost iron ore producers are being shaken out by energy prices, the same cost-curve logic threatens marginal gold, copper and lithium producers already facing AISC pressure in Q4 2026. Vale sits near the low end of the global cost curve and positions the company to benefit as higher-cost supply exits the market.

headline: MERCURIA DELIVERS 12,000 TONNES DRC COPPER TO US GOVERNMENT CRITICAL MINERALS VAULT
snippet: Commodity trading house Mercuria completed delivery of 12,000 tonnes of Democratic Republic of Congo copper to the US government's Project Vault strategic minerals program on October 16, marking one of the first significant physical copper deliveries under Washington's critical minerals diversification initiative. The DRC supplies roughly 8% of the world's mined copper and over 70% of its cobalt; securing off-take agreements there through government-backed programs represents a meaningful pivot from traditional free-market procurement toward state-sponsored supply chain building. The delivery demonstrates that Project Vault has moved from policy announcement to operational logistics.

headline: US PROJECT VAULT READIES $1B LOAN BLITZ FOR CRITICAL MINERALS MANUFACTURERS
snippet: The US government-backed Project Vault is preparing to issue up to $1 billion in subsidized loans to American manufacturers seeking access to critical minerals, escalating Washington's industrial policy push to reduce dependence on Chinese-controlled supply chains for lithium, cobalt, rare earths and other battery-critical materials. The program — backed by the DOE and Defense Logistics Agency — now stands as one of the largest government instruments actively competing with China for developing-nation mineral supply contracts, and its loan programme signals a transition from reactive policy to proactive industrial financing.

headline: BRUNSWICK EXPLORATION DRILLS 302M SPODUMENE PEGMATITE AT ANATACAU — ANAIS DYKE EXTENDS TO 500M DEPTH
snippet: Brunswick Exploration (TSX-V: BRW) reported a 302-metre spodumene-bearing pegmatite interval in drill hole AN-26-17 at its Anatacau Main project in Québec on October 15, extending the Anais dyke to approximately 500 metres vertical depth — 100 metres below the previous step-out. Visual spodumene estimates average 30% through the interval with local concentrations reaching 80%; lab assays are pending. The prior step-out hole AN-26-15 returned 202.45 metres at 1.31% Li₂O, providing the grade context for sizing this deeper extension. The lower contact of the dyke remains open in all directions, making this one of the more compelling lithium pegmatite systems advancing toward a maiden resource in eastern Canada.

headline: TECTONIC METALS HITS 10.7M AT 11.8 G/T GOLD AT FLAT, ALASKA — SEASON EXTENDS INTO LATE OCTOBER
snippet: Tectonic Metals (TSX-V: TECT) reported a 10.7-metre intersection grading 11.8 g/t gold from the Alpha Bowl zone at its Flat project in Alaska on October 16, with drilling at the Alpha Bowl and Adit areas continuing through late October as the field season extends longer than originally planned. The result adds to a growing run of high-grade intercepts at Flat — including earlier 2026 results of 1.26 metres at 15.41 g/t gold in the Alpha Bowl — and follows the 213-metre bulk-tonnage result at Freegold's adjacent Golden Summit deposit covered earlier this week. Flat is targeting a combination of near-surface bulk tonnage and high-grade underground mineralization within an underexplored orogenic gold district in western Alaska.

headline: EXIRO GROUP TAKES CONTROL OF VALE'S THOMPSON NICKEL COMPLEX — UP TO $200M INVESTMENT PLANNED
snippet: An Exiro-led consortium completed its acquisition of Vale's Thompson nickel operations in Manitoba on October 16, securing one of Canada's largest integrated nickel complexes — Thompson mine, mill, smelter and refinery — with a commitment to invest up to $200 million in modernization and expansion. The deal removes a significant non-core asset from Vale's balance sheet as the Brazilian mining giant rationalizes its portfolio. For junior mining investors, the transaction is a signal that institutional capital continues to view Canadian base-metal assets as attractively priced despite sector-wide nickel price headwinds, and that integrated processing capacity in Canada commands a strategic premium.
